definition: Duration of untreated illness is the length of time a person lives with an illness before receiving appropriate care or treatment. In this context, it refers to delays in getting mental health care for psychosis, which can be prolonged when help-seeking pathways are complex or services are hard to access.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit general definition of “duration of untreated illness” as “the length of time a person lives with an illness before receiving appropriate care or treatment,” so the first sentence’s core characterization is not directly supported.

While the packet supports that delays in receiving treatment for people with psychosis are common in LMIC settings and that care pathways are complex (often involving traditional/faith healing and non-specialist providers), it does not specifically support the added phrasing “receiving appropriate care or treatment” or that the delays are “for psychosis” in the definitional sense (it discusses psychosis contextually rather than defining the term).

The definition’s linkage to “mental health care for psychosis” and “prolonged when help-seeking pathways are complex or services are hard to access” is supported only indirectly; the packet discusses complex pathways and supply/demand factors generally, but does not state this as the definitional meaning of the term.
